- When sentiment turns negative or shows sharp decline (especially > -0.33 change), reduce forecast peak by 5–15% to avoid overshoot.
- If sentiment remains stable or mildly positive over 3+ days, allow model to hold or slightly rise, but cap upward bias at +10% above recent 7-day average.
- After a strong upward spike in sentiment (e.g., +1.00), model tends to overreact — apply downward correction of 5–10% in next 3–5 days.
- If sentiment is consistently low (avg < 0.33) or news volume is flat, model overestimates — reduce forecast by 5–10% for next 5 days.
- Mean reversion is strong in 3–5 day windows — if model is >10% above recent 7-day average, adjust downward by 2–5% per day until convergence.
- Forecast horizon 30d is prone to lag — if sentiment is trending down, model often lags by 2–4 days — adjust forecast to reflect 1–2 day lag in sentiment direction.
